rule_backend.metric_name_normalization: OpenTelemetry Prometheus-compatible translation; canonical P8 names are frozen below

dead_letter_present.customer_impact: Durable business work has exhausted automated recovery and may not complete without operator action.
safe_first_actions: Identify the durable PostgreSQL dead-letter row and owning workflow.
Do not delete or manually mark the row delivered; preserve evidence and inspect retry history.
dead_letter_present.escalation_condition: Any dead letter remains unresolved for 10 minutes, repeats after replay, or involves Finance/refund state.

stuck_saga_or_lifecycle.threshold: > 0 lifecycle transitions already classified stuck by the 15-minute watchdog boundary
stuck_saga_or_lifecycle.customer_impact: Branch lifecycle state may remain transitional and block dependent member or branch operations.
safe_first_actions: Inspect authoritative branch state and parent outbox lease before any replay.
Confirm no live worker owns the lease before using an admitted repair path.
stuck_saga_or_lifecycle.escalation_condition: A stuck transition survives one maintenance sweep or exceeds 45 minutes.

queue_oldest_age_breach.customer_impact: Asynchronous customer-visible work is falling behind its five-minute freshness objective.
safe_first_actions: Identify the bounded queue with the oldest age and verify worker availability.
Check durable PostgreSQL work before scaling or replaying delivery coordination.
queue_oldest_age_breach.escalation_condition: Oldest age exceeds 900 seconds, continues rising for 10 minutes, or affects Finance/provider reconciliation.

finance_reconciliation_mismatch.customer_impact: Recorded Finance state disagrees with expected provider/evidence state and must not be auto-corrected blindly.
safe_first_actions: Preserve Finance and provider evidence and identify the exact reconciliation class.
Stop automated mutation for the affected obligation until authoritative state is understood.
finance_reconciliation_mismatch.escalation_condition: Any mismatch persists for 5 minutes, grows, or touches issued invoices, payments, credits, or refund obligations.

provider_success_db_ack_ambiguity.customer_impact: An external provider may have succeeded while local acknowledgement is uncertain; blind retry could duplicate an external effect.
safe_first_actions: Do not blindly repeat the provider mutation.
Reconcile using provider evidence plus the fenced durable command before deciding on replay.
provider_success_db_ack_ambiguity.escalation_condition: Ambiguity remains after one reconciliation attempt or involves a monetary provider effect.

database_pool_exhaustion.threshold: >= 90% utilization or any pool timeout in 5 minutes
database_pool_exhaustion.customer_impact: Requests or workers may be unable to acquire database connections within bounded operational budgets.
safe_first_actions: Identify the saturated runtime pool and compare checked-out connections with request/worker concurrency.
Look for long transactions and dependency stalls before increasing pool size.
database_pool_exhaustion.escalation_condition: Timeouts continue for 5 minutes, utilization reaches 98%, or API readiness becomes dependency-unavailable.

database_disconnect_storm.customer_impact: Repeated database connection loss can interrupt requests and delay durable workers even when individual retries recover.
safe_first_actions: Check database reachability/TLS and pool health before restarting application processes.
Correlate disconnects with database failover, networking, and statement timeout evidence.
database_disconnect_storm.escalation_condition: Disconnect count doubles in the next 5 minutes or any production profile cannot reconnect.

redis_or_broker_unavailable.threshold: any required Redis role reports unhealthy
redis_or_broker_unavailable.customer_impact: Rate-limit/session coordination or Celery delivery may degrade; PostgreSQL durable business authority must remain intact.
safe_first_actions: Confirm the affected Redis role and TLS/auth/topology health.
Do not mutate durable PostgreSQL work to compensate for a delivery-coordination outage.
redis_or_broker_unavailable.escalation_condition: Broker remains unavailable for 5 minutes, workers cannot reconnect, or queue age starts breaching.

worker_unavailable_or_redelivery_storm.threshold: required worker profile unavailable or >= 20 redeliveries in 5 minutes
worker_unavailable_or_redelivery_storm.customer_impact: Durable asynchronous work may stop progressing or repeatedly replay after worker loss.
safe_first_actions: Identify whether worker or maintenance capacity is missing and inspect broker connectivity.
Preserve late-ack/redelivery semantics; do not force-ack durable work.
worker_unavailable_or_redelivery_storm.escalation_condition: No healthy replacement worker appears within 5 minutes or redeliveries continue rising.

duplicate_scheduler_effect_risk.threshold: any contended or unavailable Beat ownership evidence in 2 minutes
duplicate_scheduler_effect_risk.customer_impact: Scheduler ownership uncertainty can create duplicate dispatch risk; durable idempotency still prevents duplicate business authority.
safe_first_actions: Identify all Beat processes and current Redis lease ownership.
Keep duplicate schedulers fail-closed; never disable ownership fencing to restore schedules.
duplicate_scheduler_effect_risk.escalation_condition: Contention lasts more than one lease TTL or duplicate dispatch is observed.

backup_failure_or_stale_backup.threshold: > 25 hours backup age, any failure in 24 hours, or no database backup signal for 30 minutes
backup_failure_or_stale_backup.customer_impact: Recovery point objectives may no longer be trustworthy if current backups fail or become stale.
safe_first_actions: Verify backup-system evidence outside the application before declaring a successful recovery point.
Do not fabricate application-side backup success; trigger only the infrastructure-owned backup path.
backup_failure_or_stale_backup.escalation_condition: Database backup age exceeds 30 hours, two consecutive backup attempts fail, or restore verification is unavailable.

api_availability_or_latency_slo_breach.query: (doers:p8:api_availability_burn_rate:5m > 14.4 and doers:p8:api_availability_burn_rate:1h > 14.4) or (doers:p8:api_availability_burn_rate:30m > 6 and doers:p8:api_availability_burn_rate:6h > 6) or (doers:p8:api_latency_burn_rate:5m > 14.4 and doers:p8:api_latency_burn_rate:1h > 14.4) or (doers:p8:api_latency_burn_rate:30m > 6 and doers:p8:api_latency_burn_rate:6h > 6)
api_availability_or_latency_slo_breach.threshold: multi-window 14.4x fast burn or 6x slow burn against API availability/latency budgets
api_availability_or_latency_slo_breach.customer_impact: API reliability is consuming the monthly error budget too quickly through 5xx errors or requests slower than one second.
safe_first_actions: Separate availability burn from latency burn and identify the bounded route/status class driving it.
Correlate with readiness, drain, DB pool, Redis and provider signals before changing capacity.
api_availability_or_latency_slo_breach.escalation_condition: Fast burn survives 5 minutes, slow burn survives 30 minutes, or remaining monthly API budget falls below 25%.

provider_error_or_timeout_slo_breach.query: (doers:p8:provider_error_burn_rate:5m > 14.4 and doers:p8:provider_error_burn_rate:1h > 14.4) or (doers:p8:provider_error_burn_rate:30m > 6 and doers:p8:provider_error_burn_rate:6h > 6) or max(doers_provider_circuit_open) > 0
provider_error_or_timeout_slo_breach.threshold: multi-window burn against 99.5% provider success or any open provider circuit
provider_error_or_timeout_slo_breach.customer_impact: External search/notification/storage/security integrations are failing faster than the allowed provider error budget.
safe_first_actions: Identify provider/operation/outcome without exposing request or tenant identifiers in metrics.
Use durable acknowledgement/reconciliation paths; do not repeat ambiguous external effects blindly.
provider_error_or_timeout_slo_breach.escalation_condition: Fast burn persists for 5 minutes, a circuit stays open for 10 minutes, or a monetary/provider-ack ambiguity appears.

observability_pipeline_failure.threshold: missing heartbeat from any required production runtime profile for 5 minutes
observability_pipeline_failure.customer_impact: Operators may be blind to critical failures even if business processing continues, so reliability decisions cannot rely on telemetry until restored.
safe_first_actions: Verify runtime process health separately from collector/backend ingestion.
Keep business authority unchanged; restore telemetry without modifying durable PostgreSQL state.
observability_pipeline_failure.escalation_condition: Any required profile is invisible for 10 minutes or another critical incident is active while telemetry is incomplete.

api_availability.sli: non-5xx business API requests / all business API requests

api_latency.sli: business API requests completed in <= 1000 ms / all business API requests

durable_queue_freshness.sli: one-minute observations with oldest actionable queue age <= 300 seconds

lifecycle_completion.sli: one-minute observations with zero lifecycle transitions classified stuck after 900 seconds

finance_reconciliation.sli: one-minute observations with zero authoritative Finance reconciliation mismatches

provider_success_rate.sli: successful bounded provider calls / all classified provider calls

backup_freshness.sli: one-minute observations with verified database backup age <= 86400 seconds and no failed backup evidence

error_budget_policy.exhausted_budget_action: incident escalation and nonessential change freeze; never mutate business authority automatically
